steps.content: The experience so far feels more like an escape room with a haunted house theme. It's fun enough, but too many puzzles strung together get tiring. You want to take a break, but after circling the inn a few times, you still haven't found the path to town.

The fog writhes like a living thing, growing thicker, swallowing the edges of the road. A crow's hoarse cry pierces the silence, immediately followed by the rapid flapping of wings overhead. But when you turn around, there's nothing there.
The sound effects and music work together to create an immersive atmosphere. Even though you've seen far more terrifying scenes in the Black Rings, this eerie environment still gives you the creeps.

Your sense of time is distorted here. It feels like only a few dozen minutes have passed, yet darkness falls at an unnatural speed. The shadows of dead branches grow longer, twisting and writhing like countless withered arms reaching out for you...
You break a random dead branch and are surprised to find it's actually real. This place has really spared no expense on the decorations. The props are all so realistic.
Something catches your foot. As you yank it free, you hear a crescendo of childlike giggles, which then immediately disperses.
Just then, ghostly blue will-o'-the-wisps suddenly emerge in the darkness, and you realize you're standing at the edge of a desolate graveyard.
